messages:
jess_support: FYI — customer acme-inc (tenant id acme-123) opened a support ticket: their latency dashboard is missing the p95/p99 traces after the telemetry-agent rollout at ~03:10 UTC. SLO alert fired for 2 endpoints. Screenshot: https://acme.screenshots/abc123 :frowning:
michael_infra: I saw one alert too. Are p50/p90 present or is everything blank?
jess_support: p50 and p90 render fine. Only the high quantiles (95/99) are absent in both the org-level and service-level panels for that tenant. Other tenants look normal from quick checks.
@tom_reliability: Can you paste the rollout marker? Which change went out at 03:10?
sara_ops: deploy-bot: telemetry-agent v2.4.1 promoted to prod canary at 2112233300 and to prod at 2112233358. Rollout notes: normalize_labels=true enabled (ticket INF-4023).
import deploy-bot: canary -> prod completed (rollout id r-2021-11-03-03:10)
tom_reliability: OK — that config toggles normalized label keys. Dashboard queries expect `quantile` label (we historically relied on summary-derived `quantile` labels). If the agent is now converting summaries to histograms differently it might affect histogram_quantile queries.
jess_support: I ran a raw Prometheus query for the tenant: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme-123"}[5m])) by (le))` and got `result: NaN` in the API response, but the bucket series exist when I query `http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme-123"}` — the `le` values look okay.
michael_infra: paste of the raw series snippet:
```
http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme-123",le="0.1",instance="m1"} 12345
http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme-123",le="0.25",instance="m1"} 23456
http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme-123",le="+Inf",instance="m1"} 30000
```
But dashboard panels are doing `by (service,quantile)` queries — if the agent dropped the `quantile` label in summary->quantile translation then panels will show nothing.
tom_reliability: That matches. I queried `/api/v1/series?match[]=http_request_duration_seconds{tenant="acme-123"}` and noticed summaries now report only `_sum/_count` and the quantile label no longer present (agent changed summary export). Other tenants on older agent still have quantile series.
jess_support: Customer is asking for ETA. They rely on p95/p99 for incident mgmt.
michael_infra: Short-term workaround: edit affected dashboard panels to use `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme-123"}[5m])) by (le, service))` — that avoids `quantile` label dependency. I'll open a patch for that across customer-specific dashboards.
tom_reliability: Long-term we should either revert the normalize_labels toggle or update agent to synthesize `quantile` series for summaries. Recommend rolling back the prod rollout of v2.4.1 while we patch dashboards and agent behavior. +page for change control.
sara_ops: Initiating rollback for telemetry-agent r-2021-11-03-03:10 to v2.4.0 on acme-affecting shards. Action id: rollback-2112233505. ETA ~12m.
import deploy-bot: rollback started (rollback-2112233505) — removing normalize_labels on affected hosts.
michael_infra: I'll push a safe dashboard patch (query variant) for acme tenant as a stopgap, and then coordinate with tom on the agent fix. Creating infra ticket INF-4030 and dashboard task DASH-789.
jess_support: Thanks — told customer we expect restored percentiles within ~20m (rollback + dashboard patch). I'll keep them updated. :thumbsup:
tom_reliability: After rollback please re-run the histogram_quantile query and paste results. If `quantile` series return, we can close the incident. Also add note to release notes about summary->quantile behavior change.
jess_support: Will follow up once rollback completes and I re-check. Inc ticket #SUP-9122 created and linked to INF-4030.
